title: Microsoft Edge: top sites in the Edge search bar
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts and both documented policy controls check out. It correctly distinguishes the search bar feature's unpublished default and licensing from the existing policies, and reports the policy page's conflicting Microsoft-account applicability statements.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether search bar top sites appear by default.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge search bar Top Sites default rollout version' and 'Microsoft Edge Top Sites search bar default rollout browsing history version channel'; read the roadmap and both quick-links policy pages. Their default statements concern the new tab page, not search bar top sites.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the licence or plan covering this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge for Business free license', 'Microsoft Edge licensing browser requirements', and 'Microsoft Edge top sites search bar license pricing NewTabPageManagedQuickLinks NewTabPageQuickLinksEnabled'; read Edge for Business and both policy pages. No applicable entitlement was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge for Business free license'; read the supplied roadmap, NewTabPageQuickLinksEnabled, NewTabPageManagedQuickLinks and Microsoft Edge for Business in full. None names a licence covering search bar top sites.

claims.claim: The policy pages do not state the Edge version or release channel that first shows search bar top sites.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge search bar Top Sites default rollout version' and 'Microsoft Edge Top Sites search bar default rollout browsing history version channel'; read both quick-links policy pages. Their supported versions apply to the existing policies, not the new search bar feature.

claims.claim: The sources do not state how rollout of the search bar top sites feature is staged.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge search bar Top Sites default rollout version' and 'Microsoft Edge Top Sites search bar default rollout browsing history version channel'; read the roadmap and both quick-links policy pages. None states tenant, profile or channel rollout staging for this feature.

claims.claim: Neither policy page describes a control governing only the search bar top sites list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge search bar top sites policy hide browsing history' and 'top sites search bar hide policy users'; read both quick-links policies and matching Edge policy-index excerpts. Both documented controls also govern new tab page quick links.

claims.claim: The policy pages document no setting preventing users from hiding the top sites list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'top sites search bar hide policy users'; read both quick-links policy references. Mandatory managed tiles cannot be deleted, but neither page says users can be prevented from hiding the list; QuickLinksEnabled explicitly does not force quick links to be visible.
